subject: DPA negotiation: breach-notification timing, subprocessors & DocuSign execution
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: DPA redline & breach-notification timing

Sarah —

Thanks again for the readiness call yesterday. Attached is our suggested redline to Acme's DPA (DPA_redline_Marissa_v1.docx). Two sticking points from our side we wanted to flag up-front: breach notification timing and subprocessor termination/notice.

Proposal summary:
- Initial incident notification: 48 hours from confirmed impact to Acme customer data (we can provide a phone escalation for P1 only).
- Full remediation report and root-cause analysis: within 7 business days where possible.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide a current subprocessor list and commit to 30 days' notice before onboarding a new subprocessor relevant to Acme.

If these sound reasonable, we can push DPA_Final_v3 to DocuSign and you can countersign. I’ve copied Mina (Legal) and Neha (Security) for any legal/technical clarifications.

Attachments: DPA_redline_Marissa_v1.docx

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Delgado <tom.delgado@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 11:00:00 -0000
Subject: Re: DPA redline & breach-notification timing

Marissa —

Thanks for the redline. Quick read: Acme’s security/compliance team is asking for a more aggressive notification window. Specifically: initial notification within 24 hours of discovery and a phone escalation immediately for incidents that materially affect customer data. They also want explicit rights to terminate for cause if a subprocessor is engaged and cannot be removed within 30 days.

I attached our version for reference (ACME_DPA_redline.docx). Also please send the current subprocessor list and confirm what transfer mechanisms Redwood relies on for EU/UK transfers.

We'd like DocuSign ready once we align on these points.

—Sarah
Sarah Turner
Head of Legal Operations, Acme Corp
sarah.turner@acme-corp.com
Attachment: ACME_DPA_redline.docx
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@acme-corp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 12:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: DPA redline & breach-notification timing

Sarah —

Appreciate the quick review and the ACME redline. A few points from Redwood Legal & Security:

1) Notification timing: Our standard position is initial notification "as soon as reasonably possible" and within 72 hours for confirmed breaches. That said, we understand Acme's operational needs and can offer a negotiated compromise: initial notification within 48 hours for confirmed incidents that impact Acme data; for suspected incidents we will notify within 72 hours of confirmation of suspected impact.

2) Two-tier approach:
- P1 / confirmed exfiltration affecting Acme production data: initial notification within 24 hours and immediate phone escalation.
- P2 / confirmed but contained impact: initial notification within 48 hours.

3) Full report and remediation plan: target within 7 business days; interim updates at 72-hour cadence while investigation is active.

4) Subprocessors & transfers: Redwood publishes a current subprocessor list (link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/subprocessor-list-v2.pdf). For transfers we rely on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses plus the UK Addendum; where additional safeguards are required we can agree to implement reasonable technical/organizational measures and provide a data-transfer addendum.

5) Termination for cause: we cannot accept a unilateral termination right for routine subprocessor additions; we can commit to 30 days' notice and the ability for Acme to object in writing. If a substantiated security/contractual risk is identified and cannot be mitigated within a mutually agreed period, parties will work in good faith on remedial steps up to termination.

If Acme needs a firmer 24-hour SLA across the board, we will need explicit carve-outs for law enforcement coordination and in-flight investigations where disclosure could impede response.

I’ve attached a redline that implements the compromise language (DPA_Final_v3.docx). If the compromise is acceptable, Marissa — can you confirm and I’ll prepare the DocuSign envelope.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
Attachment: DPA_Final_v3.docx
From: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@acme-corp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 08:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: DPA redline & breach-notification timing

Mina —

Thanks for the detailed note. Acme can accept the two-tier approach with the following change requests:
- Make the 48-hour timeline a firm contractual obligation for confirmed incidents (no "as soon as reasonably possible" language).
- Add a short clause that permits Acme to terminate for cause if a subprocessor creates an unmitigable risk and Redwood fails to remediate within 30 days.

If you can accept those two clean edits I will route the DPA to our signatory and we will complete DocuSign the same day.

Tom Delgado (copied) will be our technical point for any subprocessor objections.

—Sarah
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 09:10:00 -0000
Subject: Re: DPA redline & breach-notification timing

Looping in Rishi for final approval on the spot concessions. Proposed compromise for Acme:
- Initial notification: 48 hours for confirmed incidents (contractual).
- For P1 confirmed exfiltration: initial operational alert within 24 hours and phone escalation; contractual language to reflect phone escalation for P1 only.
- Full remediation report: 7 business days; interim updates every 72 hours.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will continue the 30-day notice policy; allow Acme written objection; if unmitigable, parties will negotiate remediation or termination rights per the language Mina proposed.

I will issue the DocuSign envelope once we have Rishi's okay. Link to envelope (to be sent when ready): https://docusign.net/envelope/0x12345

Marissa
